result.title: Weight Decay and Neuron Condensation: A Three-Stage Analysis of Two-Layer ReLU Networks
result.summary: Weight decay is widely used as a regularization technique in neural network training, yet its role in neuron condensation (parameter direction alignment) remains unclear. Starting from a parameter initialization in the neural tangent kernel regime, we characterize training dynamics under weight decay through three stages: rapid fitting, amplitude compression, and neuron condensation. Using a two-layer ReLU network, we analyze a residual correlation field that governs both neuron amplitudes and directions. During rapid fitting, the residual approaches a quasi-static equilibrium maintained by weight decay while the tangent kernel remains nearly unchanged. In the early stage of amplitude compression, kernel decay amplifies the residual correlation field, whose isolated attracting extrema provide candidates for condensation directions. As neuron amplitudes stabilize, we bound the drift of attracting extrema and demonstrate contraction of neuron directions around them, leading to neuron condensation. This staged analysis provides a dynamical understanding of how weight decay promotes a condensed representation, beyond reducing parameter norms.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用两层 ReLU 网络分析权重衰减下的训练动力学，划分为快速拟合、幅度压缩和神经元凝聚三阶段，借助残差相关场刻画神经元幅度与方向的演化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“表示向少数吸引方向收缩凝聚”的动力学分析，可能为理解 LVR 中 latent 状态表示为何坍缩到有限方向、以及表示几何与容量代价提供概念类比，但缺乏视觉与推理环节，需较多核查。
